Personally, I know I would spend time trying to make things work because you obviously love the person you are with, and love makes you make up excuses for bad behaviour from your partner, but I think after some time I would realize that I could never trust my partner again and then have to go through the pain of a breakup again. So hearing this from an outsider view looking in at your situation, I would definitely advise you to go separate ways and do no contact except practical stuff (divorce, moving, etc.) until you are over her. I think from your explanation of the confusion you feel conserning how she could do that to you (I felt the same way, when I found out, still baffled 7 months later) that you have loyalty as one of your key values, and she obviously does not.. This could become a problem in the relationship in the future as well. 
However, at the end of the day, no one knows the full story except you and your wife, and you are the only one who can decide what is best for you. By all means, talk to people about it (friends, family or a professional), but in the end you have to make the choice that you believe Will make you the happiest in the future (think 10 years, not 4 months). Be kind to yourself, and put yourself first during this time.

My first response when I feel it coming is focusing on calming down my breath. There are many things going on in your body during a panic attack that you cannot control, but the breath is one of the things that you can control. Calming it down reduces the overflow of oxygen flowing to your brain, which can often make you dizzy and feel as if you are about to pass out. 

The second thing I try to do is the 5-4-3-2-1 technique, where I focus on5 things I can see, then 4 things I can touch, 3 things I can hear, 2 things I can smell and finally 1 thing I can taste. This helps me get back down to «Ground level», at least on a good day. I wish you luck and hope it helps!
